arxiv-2112-08381.title: Testing the universality of cosmic-ray nuclei from protons to oxygen with AMS-02
arxiv-2112-08381.creator: Michael Korsmeier, Alessandro Cuoco
arxiv-2112-08381.description: Abstract The AMS-02 experiment has provided high-precision measurements of several cosmic-ray (CR) species. The achieved percent-level accuracy gives access to small spectral differences among the different species and, in turn, this allows scrutinizing the universality of CR acceleration, which is expected in the standard scenario of CR shock acceleration.

arxiv-2211-00064.title: KILLING OPERATOR FOR THE KERR METRIC
arxiv-2211-00064.creator: J.-F. Pommaret
arxiv-2211-00064.description: Abstract ABSTRACT When {\cal{D}}:E\rightarrow F is a linear differential operator of order q between the sections of vector bundles over a manifold X of dimension n , it is defined by a bundle map \Phi:J_{q}(E)\rightarrow F=F_{0} that may depend, explicitly or implicitly, on constant parameters a,b,c,... .

arxiv-2304-14228.title: Optical variability in Quasars: Scalings with black hole mass and Eddington ratio depend on the observed timescales 2023 Optical variability in Quasars: Scalings with black hole mass and Eddington ratio depend on the observed timescales – 7
arxiv-2304-14228.creator: P. Arévalo, P. Lira, P. Sánchez-Sáez, P. Patel, E. López-Navas, E. Churazov, L. Hernández-García
arxiv-2304-14228.description: Abstract Quasars emission is highly variable, and this variability gives us clues to understand the accretion process onto supermassive black holes. We can expect variability properties to correlate with the main physical properties of the accreting black hole, i.e., its mass and accretion rate. It has been established that the relative amplitude of variability anti-correlates with the accretion rate.

arxiv-2308-01165.title: Termination in Concurrency, Revisited Conference: International Symposium on Principles and Practice of Declarative Programming; October 22–23, 2023; Lisboa, Portugal International Symposium on Principles and Practice of Declarative Programming (PPDP 2023), October 22–23, 2023, Lisboa, Portugal Pric
arxiv-2308-01165.creator: Joseph W. N. Paulus, Jorge A. Pérez, Daniele Nantes-Sobrinho
arxiv-2308-01165.description: Abstract . Termination is a central property in sequential programming models: a term is terminating if all its reduction sequences are finite. Termination is also important in concurrency in general, and for message-passing programs in particular. A variety of type systems that enforce termination by typing have been developed.

The South Pole Telescope third-generation camera (SPT-3G) has observed over 10 000 10\,000 square degrees of sky at 95, 150, and 220 GHz (3.3, 2.0, 1.4 mm, respectively) overlapping the ongoing 14 000 14\,000 square-degree Euclid Wide Survey. arxiv-2507-23212.title: Hierarchical Triples vs. Globular Clusters: Binary black hole merger eccentricity distributions compete and evolve with redshift 2015 Hierarchical Triples vs. Globular Clusters: Binary black hole merger eccentricity distributions compete and evolve with redshift – 9
arxiv-2507-23212.creator: Andris Dorozsmai, Isobel M. Romero-Shaw, Aditya Vijaykumar, Silvia Toonen, Fabio Antonini, Kyle Kremer, Michael Zevin, Evgeni Grishin
arxiv-2507-23212.description: Abstract The formation mechanisms of merging binary black holes (BBHs) observed by the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA collaboration remain uncertain. Detectable eccentricity provides a powerful diagnostic for distinguishing between different formation channels, but resolving their eccentricity distributions requires the detection of a large number of eccentric mergers.

arxiv-2508-04865.title: Agnostics: Learning to Code in Any Programming Language via Reinforcement with a Universal Learning Environment
arxiv-2508-04865.creator: Aleksander Boruch-Gruszecki, Yangtian Zi, Zixuan Wu, Tejas Oberoi, Carolyn Jane Anderson, Joydeep Biswas, Arjun Guha
arxiv-2508-04865.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) already excel at writing code in high-resource languages such as Python and JavaScript, yet stumble on low-resource languages that remain essential to science and engineering. Besides the obvious shortage of pre-training data, post-training itself is a bottleneck: every new language seems to require new datasets, test harnesses, and reinforcement-learning (RL) infrastructure.

pmc-11509861.creator: Shichun He, Zaimei Yuan, Sifan Dai, Zibei Wang, Shusheng Zhao, Bin Zhang, Huaming Mao, Dongwang Wu, Todd Riley Callaway
pmc-11509861.description: Yaks are one of the important livestock on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, providing abundant dairy and meat products for the local people. The formation of these dairy and meat products mainly relies on the microbiota in their gastrointestinal tract, which digests and metabolizes plant feed.

pmc-11723654.title: Gender-specification lifestyle factors associated with mild cognitive impairment among young-old adults in Taiwan
pmc-11723654.creator: Su-Wen Chuang, Ching-Wen Chen, Meng-Chang Lee, Yu-Hsuan Chen, Wen Su, Cheng-Jung Chen, Wei-Teing Chen, Po-Jen Hsiao, Chih-Chien Chiu, Sui-Lung Su
pmc-11723654.description: Background: The prevalence of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) exhibits a positive correlation with age, particularly evident in the old-old female population. Lifestyle factors have been identified as crucial risk determinants for MCI. However, there is a scarcity of research focusing on lifestyle factors among young-old population.

pmc-12427564.title: Development of IVF Porcine Embryos in Microwell Culture System
pmc-12427564.creator: Kayode Balogun, Zoltan Machaty, Dariusz Skarzynski, Szilárd Bodó, Vass Nóra, Gabriella Kútvölgyi, Tamas Somfai
pmc-12427564.description: Simple SummaryThe efficiency of producing porcine embryos in a laboratory by in vitro fertilization (IVF) is notoriously low. Our understanding of the relevant factors contributing to this low efficacy is limited, in part, by the difficulty of tracking the development of individual embryos.

pmc-12466893.title: Does the Maternal Gut Microbiome Influence the Outcome of Perinatal Asphyxia?
pmc-12466893.creator: Vlad-Petru Morozan, Mara I. Ionescu, Carmen M. D. Zahiu, Ana Maria Catrina, Andreea Racoviță, Ana-Teodora Chirilă, Ioana-Alexandra Dogaru, Cristian Ciotei, Gratiela Gradisteanu Pircalabioru, Ana-Maria Zăgrean
pmc-12466893.description: This review explores the maternal gut microbiome’s role in shaping neonatal neurodevelopmental outcomes following perinatal asphyxia (PA), a leading cause of infant mortality and disability with limited therapeutic options beyond hypothermia. We synthesized current evidence on microbiome-mediated neuroprotective mechanisms against hypoxic-ischemic brain injury.

pmc-12978927.title: Knowledge-Guided Explainable Recommendation Tool for Cancer Risk Prediction Models Using Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models: Development and Validation Study
pmc-12978927.creator: Shumin Ren, Xin Zheng, Jing Zhao, Jiale Du, Yuxin Zhang, Cheng Bi, Jie Song, Jinyi Zhang, Hongmei Lang, Fan Zhang, Bairong Shen, Andrew Coristine
pmc-12978927.description: BackgroundCancer risk prediction models are vital for precision prevention, enabling individualized assessment of cancer susceptibility based on genetic, clinical, environmental, and lifestyle factors. However, the practical use of these models is hindered by fragmented resources, heterogeneous reporting, and the absence of transparent, structured systems for systematic discovery and comparison.

pmc-13026399.title: Neonatal Sepsis: Pathogens, Clinical Challenges, and Emerging Solutions
pmc-13026399.creator: Matthew Green, Jyotsna Chawla, Cyril Blavo
pmc-13026399.description: Neonatal sepsis remains a major cause of preventable newborn deaths worldwide despite advances in maternal screening, antibiotic use, and neonatal care. Persistent diagnostic delays, rising antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and unequal access to resources highlight the urgent need for new approaches.

pmc-13081257.title: Evaluating the performance of ancient DNA genetic relatedness estimation methods using high-fidelity pedigree simulations
pmc-13081257.creator: Maël Lefeuvre, Marie-Claude Marsolier, Céline Bon
pmc-13081257.description: BackgroundRecent advancements in paleogenetics, coupled with the emergence of dedicated statistical methods have, in recent years, streamlined the detection of close genetic ties from ancient DNA samples, leading to a substantial surge in scientific publications emphasising the reconstruction of genealogies within archaeological funerary contexts.

pmc-13226797.title: Factors influencing fear of falling among community-dwelling older women living alone based on the senescent sleep model: A descriptive correlational study
pmc-13226797.creator: Young Joo Lee, Yong Soon Shin
pmc-13226797.description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate sleep quality and the fear of falling among community-dwelling older women living alone and to identify the factors influencing the fear of falling. MethodsThis descriptive correlational study included 178 community-dwelling older women living alone. Data were collected from December 10, 2023, to February 29, 2024.

pmc-13235850.title: Rectal cancer in the era of precision oncology: more options, more uncertainty
pmc-13235850.creator: Reza Mirnezami
pmc-13235850.description: ciding which of several competing strategies should be pursued. pmc-13517918.title: Pulmonary Toxicity and Biodistribution of Sodium Fluoride in Male Rats Following Intratracheal Instillation and Nose-Only Inhalation Exposure
pmc-13517918.creator: Tanya Bhatt, Dong Hyun Kim, Soyeon Jeon, Se-Hwan Choi, Jaebaek Jang, Mihye Kwon, Jang Woo Park, Min-Seok Kim, Iljung Lee, Wan-Seob Cho
pmc-13517918.description: Pulmonary exposure to sodium fluoride (NaF) may occur in certain consumer-product and occupational settings, but its pulmonary toxicity and systemic biodistribution remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated acute pulmonary inflammatory responses and biodistribution kinetics in rats following a single airway exposure to NaF. Non-radioactive NaF was administered in 7-week-old male Sprague-Dawley rats by intratracheal instillation at 0.75, 1.5, or 3.

pmc-13623611.title: Toward standardized continuous glucose monitoring validation: lessons from the Sinocare iCan i3 accuracy study
pmc-13623611.creator: Auda Ameur
pmc-13623611.description: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has transformed diabetes management by providing real-time glucose measurements and supporting improved glycemic control. Consequently, the methodological quality of CGM accuracy studies has become increasingly important for clinicians, regulatory agencies, and healthcare decision-makers. The recent real-world evaluation of the Sinocare iCan i3 CGM system provides valuable evidence regarding device performance under routine clinical conditions.
